children: Well-known investor Ashish Dhawan picked up an additional stake of more than 1 percent in financial services company Religare Enterprises for the second consecutive session through open-market transactions on August 31.

After Dhawan bought a stake in the company on Friday, the stock reacted strongly on Monday, rising 4.18 percent to Rs 242.80 amid heavy volumes on the National Stock Exchange and witnessing a breakout from consolidation.

Dhawan bought more than 36 lakh shares, representing 1.05 percent of the paid-up equity, in Religare for Rs 85.3 crore at a price of Rs 237 per share. This was in addition to the 1.11 percent stake he purchased on Friday.
The two transactions increased his stake in Religare Enterprises to more than 7 percent, compared with the 5.24 percent stake he held as of June 2026.
DSP Mutual Fund raises stake in Concord Biotech

DSP Mutual Fund acquired an additional 12.88 lakh shares, representing 1.23 percent of the paid-up equity, in Ahmedabad-headquartered biotechnology company Concord Biotech for Rs 180.86 crore at Rs 1,404.1 per share. The fund already held a 1.75 percent stake in the company as of June 2026.

However, Canadian corporate entity 1575773 Ontario Inc exited Concord Biotech by selling its entire holding of 20.92 lakh shares, representing a 2 percent stake, at the same price, for Rs 293.78 crore.
Concord Biotech shares fell 2.36 percent to Rs 1,446.1 on the NSE, extending their decline for the fourth consecutive session.
Jainam Broking buys 0.65% stake in Shreeji Shipping Global from promoters

Gujarat-headquartered Jainam Broking acquired 10.62 lakh shares, equivalent to a 0.65 percent stake, in Shreeji Shipping Global from the promoters for Rs 68.53 crore. The shares were acquired at Rs 645.3 per share.
Promoters Ashokkumar Haridas Lal and Lal Jitendra Haridas each sold 5.31 lakh shares for Rs 34.26 crore. The stock ended at Rs 644.6 on the NSE, down 1.21 percent amid high volumes.
BlackRock sells 0.76% stake in PTC India

iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF, managed by BlackRock through its subsidiary BlackRock Fund Advisors, offloaded 22.69 lakh shares, representing a 0.76 percent stake in PTC India, for Rs 34.3 crore at a price of Rs 151.17 per share.
BlackRock offloads over 1% stake in SBI Card
BNP Paribas Financial Markets acquired 97.83 lakh shares, representing a 1.02 percent stake, in SBI Cards & Payment Services for Rs 632.07 crore at a price of Rs 646.04 per share.

However, BlackRock International sold 52.86 lakh shares in SBI Cards & Payment Services for Rs 342.41 crore at a price of Rs 647.68 per share, while BlackRock Global Funds offloaded 49.98 lakh shares at Rs 644.75 per share, valued at Rs 322.3 crore.
The two BlackRock transactions together represented a 1.08 percent stake worth Rs 664.72 crore.
BlackRock buys Rs 445 crore worth of shares in Ather Energy

BlackRock Global Funds bought 25.99 lakh shares, representing 0.65 percent of the paid-up equity, in Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy for Rs 445.31 crore at a price of Rs 1,713.02 per share.

Ather Energy shares soared 6.27 percent to end at a record high of Rs 1,717.7 on the NSE, accompanied by heavy volumes. The sharp rise may have followed promoter entity Hero MotoCorp’s acquisition on Friday of an additional 3.01 percent stake from the Government of Singapore for Rs 1,758.24 crore.
BNP Paribas picks up 0.52% stake in Balkrishna Industries
BNP Paribas Financial Markets picked up 10.2 lakh shares, equivalent to a 0.52 percent stake in tyre maker Balkrishna Industries, for Rs 232.68 crore at a price of Rs 2,281.04 per share.
BNP Paribas buys Rs 568 crore worth of shares in Astral
BNP Paribas Financial Markets acquired 37.33 lakh shares, representing a 1.39 percent stake, in building materials company Astral at Rs 1,522.79 per share, valued at Rs 568.46 crore.
Meanwhile, Societe Generale picked up 13.5 lakh shares, representing a 0.5 percent stake, in Astral for Rs 206.17 crore at a price of Rs 1,526.56 per share.

title: Ashish Dhawan buys additional over 1% stake in Religare Enterprises for second consecutive session
